question:
A linear coding rule assigns a real output to every real input according to the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ defined by $f(x)=3-4x$. Students are asked to determine whether this rule gives a unique output for each distinct input and whether every real number can occur as an output. Because both the domain and codomain are $\mathbb{R}$, they must work with arbitrary real numbers rather than only test a few numerical cases. For surjectivity, an arbitrary element $y$ of the codomain may be chosen and the equation $f(x)=y$ solved for $x$.

(a) Find $f(-1)$ and $f(2)$.

(b) If $f(x_1)=f(x_2)$, show that $x_1=x_2$.

(c) For an arbitrary $y\in\mathbb{R}$, find a real number $x$ satisfying $f(x)=y$.

(d) Hence classify $f$ with respect to the one-one and onto properties.
explanation:
(a)
$f(-1)=3-4(-1)=7$ and $f(2)=3-8=-5$.

(b)
Suppose $f(x_1)=f(x_2)$. Then $3-4x_1=3-4x_2$. Subtracting $3$ from both sides gives $-4x_1=-4x_2$, and hence $x_1=x_2$. Therefore, $f$ is one-one.

(c)
Let $y\in\mathbb{R}$. We require $3-4x=y$. Thus $-4x=y-3$, giving $x=\frac{3-y}{4}$. Since $y$ is real, $\frac{3-y}{4}$ is also real. Therefore, every $y\in\mathbb{R}$ has a pre-image.

(d)
Part (b) shows that $f$ is one-one, while part (c) shows that every element of the codomain has a pre-image, so $f$ is onto. Therefore, $f$ is both one-one and onto.

options.A: $f(-1)=7$ and $f(2)=-5$; equality of images implies $x_1=x_2$, and every $y\in\mathbb{R}$ has the pre-image $x=\frac{3-y}{4}$. Hence, $f$ is both one-one and onto.
options.B: $f(-1)=-1$ and $f(2)=5$; $f$ is one-one but not onto because negative real numbers have no pre-images.
options.C: $f(-1)=7$ and $f(2)=-5$; every $y\in\mathbb{R}$ has the pre-image $x=\frac{y-3}{4}$, so $f$ is onto but not one-one.
options.D: $f(-1)=-7$ and $f(2)=11$; distinct real inputs can have the same image, and some real numbers have no pre-images, so $f$ is neither one-one nor onto.
